item.title: New US Residential Construction Slows in Broad-Based Decline
item.description: New residential construction in the US declined in July as single-family starts slid to the slowest pace since 2022.

item.title: US 10-Year Yields Climb to Highest Since 2025 as Rout Deepens
item.description: A deepening global bond selloff sent the US benchmark yield to the highest since early 2025, as thin August trading met investors wary of inflation and a deluge of corporate debt supply.

item.title: Top East Africa Bourse Plans ETF Push to Tap Investor Demand
item.description: East Africa’s biggest bourse plans to offer a variety of exchange-traded funds to meet demand from investors, Nairobi Securities Exchange Chief Executive Officer Frank Mwiti said.

item.title: South Africa Proposes Sweeping Changes to Power-Price Framework
item.description: South Africa proposed sweeping changes to its electricity-tariff framework, the biggest overhaul of its pricing policy in almost two decades.

item.title: India’s Digital Payments Boom Fails to Dent Demand for Cash
item.description: India’s rapid adoption of digital payments has failed to curb demand for cash, making it harder to predict how much currency will be needed, Reserve Bank of India Deputy Governor Shirish Chandra Murmu said.

item.title: AI Election Backlash Is Shaping Wall Street’s Stock Market Views
item.description: The backlash against artificial intelligence and the data centers needed to run it is becoming such a touchy election issue that Wall Street is being forced to factor it into its stock market recommendations.

item.title: US Shale’s Metamorphosis Is a Lesson for Big Tech
item.description: Drillers’ wild spending spree of the 2010s is a cautionary tale for the likes of Amazon and Meta.

item.title: Klarna Cuts Revenue Guidance and Is Searching for New CFO
item.description: Klarna Group Plc cut its expectations for how much revenue it will generate this year, citing foreign exchange pressures and volumes in Germany, even as it reported a profit beat for the second straight quarter.

item.title: Alibaba-Backed AI Video Platform ShengShu Mulls HK IPO
item.description: ShengShu Technology, an artificial intelligence video platform backed by Alibaba Group Holding Ltd., is considering a Hong Kong initial public offering, according to people familiar with the matter.

item.title: Staffing Stocks Defy Gravity After Analysts Warned of AI Demise
item.description: Professional staffing firms are flying high in the stock market, with some on pace for their best performance in years despite analysts’ concerns that artificial intelligence would cause their downfall.

item.title: Ant Group Said to Sell 3% Paytm Stake in $309 Million Deal
item.description: Resilient Asset Management BV, controlled by Paytm founder Vijay Shekhar Sharma, on Tuesday sold a 3% stake in the Indian fintech for $309 million, according to a person familiar with the matter, who asked not to be identified.

item.title: Pimco’s Stracke Says Wealth Firms Running Shy of Private Credit
item.description: Wealth managers are beating a retreat from private credit and ramping up a search for alternatives, as they continue to reel from sudden exit restrictions at several major direct lending funds earlier this year.

item.title: Intesa’s SpaceX Stake Worth Almost $1 Billion at End of June
item.description: Intesa Sanpaolo SpA owned about $966 million in SpaceX shares at the end of June, according to a regulatory filing detailing the holding for the first time.

item.title: Integral AI’s Demise Signals Hurdles Ahead for Robotics
item.description: It may cost too much to develop robots for simple tasks

item.title: Texas Stock Exchange Lures Two ETFs in First Primary Listings
item.description: The Texas Stock Exchange notched its first primary listings as two small exchange-traded funds focused on the state’s economy announced plans to transfer to the upstart marketplace.

item.title: Data Center Gas Plants to Boost US Power Emissions by 20%
item.description: Data center developers are turning to bespoke natural-gas power plants, a development that promises to dramatically increase carbon emissions and make it harder for US technology companies to meet their lofty climate goals.

item.title: Mexico and rail route to avoid Panama Canal
item.description: The land-based alternative isn’t new, but the opportunities to avoid the Panama Canal are greater than ever

item.title: Bessent’s Japan Yen Move Echoes Past US Currency Interventions
item.description: Turning points in major currencies sometimes followed notable policymaker interventions.

item.title: Emerging Assets Halt Rally on Higher Oil Prices, Bond Selloff
item.description: An emerging-markets equity benchmark snapped a four-day advance and a currency gauge retreated from record highs as a global bond selloff combined with higher oil prices weighed on risk sentiment.

item.title: India Challenges US Quartz Tariffs With WTO Consultation Bid
item.description: India has sought consultations with the US at the World Trade Organization over tariffs imposed by the White House on some quartz products, adding another point of friction between the two countries as they remain without a trade deal.

item.title: AI Is Starting to Create Jobs in the UK
item.description: Most British businesses say artificial intelligence has created new roles, a Lloyds survey found.

item.title: Bond Yields Are Hitting Multidecade Highs Around the World
item.description: Everything from inflation to the AI boom is pushing borrowing costs higher.

item.title: RBI’s Forex Deposit U-Turn Exposes Wider Communication Gap
item.description: A sudden decision by India’s central bank to end a special incentive for attracting foreign-currency deposits a month ahead of schedule has caught bankers, economists and traders off guard and raised questions about how effectively it was communicating with market participants.

item.title: Alibaba-Backed Robot Maker LimX Said to Plan Up to $300 Million Hong Kong IPO
item.description: LimX Dynamics has confidentially filed for a Hong Kong initial public offering to raise as much as $300 million, people familiar with the matter said, adding to a wave of Chinese robotics companies lining up to go public.

item.title: Tata Sons Defers Annual Shareholder Meeting for Lack of Quorum
item.description: Tata Sons Pvt. deferred its annual general meeting after a key shareholder was unable to participate, according to people familiar with the matter, even as the Indian conglomerate prepares to find a new chairman following Natarajan Chandrasekaran’s resignation last week.

item.title: Mark Cuban-Backed ‘Physical AI’ Startup Nears $500 Million SPAC Deal
item.description: A startup backed by Mark Cuban that makes hardware and software used to more safely control and operate autonomous robots plans to go public via a blank-check vehicle in a deal valuing it at $500 million.

item.title: Rare $1 Billion IPO Rush Seen in Zambia After Election
item.description: Zambia’s stock exchange expects to bring a record $1 billion of initial public offerings to market after this month’s presidential election, as Africa’s second-biggest copper producer benefits from soaring prices for the metal.

item.title: Robot Dogs Make Chinese Billionaire Even Richer Despite US Curbs
item.description: Wang Xingxing, a millennial billionaire at the center of China’s AI push, is set to see his fortune soar even as Washington blocks his company from launching new robot models in the US.

item.title: Ardian Taps UBS to Explore Sale of Swissbit
item.description: Ardian is weighing a potential sale of Swissbit, a provider of industrial data storage and security products, people familiar with the matter said.

item.title: Pony AI’s Robotaxi Revenue Reaches Record as Sales Jump 69%
item.description: Pony AI Inc.’s robotaxi sales reached a quarterly high, now accounting for a third of total revenue, with overseas momentum continuing to accelerate.
